q4.answer: Payment charges only on a StockReserved event, and on nothing else. StockReserved exists only after Inventory's conditional update succeeded, so the card is never charged without reserved stock. Payment also needs a payment_requests row (from OrderPlaced); if it is missing the handler throws and no charge is made.

q5.answer: Each service writes its result event to its own outbox table in the same transaction as its state change. Its relay then publishes it to order-events, keyed by orderId. If the service crashes between commit and publish, the outbox row is already committed, so the relay publishes it after restart. Delivery is at-least-once, and consumers cope with duplicates.

q6.answer: Every consumer inserts the eventId into processed_events (unique key) in the same transaction as its work. A second delivery hits the unique key, so it changes nothing, writes no outbox row and just acks. A second guard on the business key (one reservation and one payment per orderId, status change only from PENDING) covers the same event under a new eventId.

q7.answer: The charge uses the idempotency key charge:{orderId}, built from the order and not from the event. After the crash nothing was committed, so the redelivered StockReserved reruns the handler. It sends the same key, and the provider returns the first result without charging again. Payment then writes its result.

q9.answer: The PaymentDeclined event that Payment publishes causes the release, and Inventory releases it. Inventory consumes PaymentDeclined and, if the reservation is RESERVED, sets it to RELEASED and restores the stock in one transaction. If it is already RELEASED or missing, it only records processed_events and acks.

q10.answer: Order Service consumes StockRejected, PaymentSucceeded and PaymentDeclined. In one transaction it updates orders.status from PENDING to CONFIRMED or CANCELLED (WHERE status = 'PENDING'), inserts processed_events, and writes an OrderConfirmed or OrderCancelled outbox row. If the order is not PENDING, zero rows change and it still acks.

q11.answer: The OrderConfirmed or OrderCancelled event that Order Service publishes through its outbox after the status commit triggers the email, and Notification consumes it. Notification claims an email_log row (unique on orderId and type) before sending. If the email cannot be sent, Notification logs it and returns normally, with no retry and no DLQ entry, and the order status is not touched.
